_meta.notes: MTDC = Maharashtra Tourism Development Corporation (runs resorts + water sports). Konkan coast = the western coastal strip (Raigad, Ratnagiri, Sindhudurg dists). Many hill forts are steep unmaintained climbs -- safety content must reflect that. Ajanta/Ellora/Elephanta + the Western Ghats sites are UNESCO listed.

destinationsScraped.name: Ajanta Caves
destinationsScraped.url: https://maharashtratourism.gov.in/cave/ajanta/ (read via in-app browser; WebFetch on the gov site returns navigation-only)
destinationsScraped.summary: ~30 Buddhist rock-cut caves in a horseshoe gorge above the Waghora river, Sahyadri hills, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) district. Two phases: early group ~2nd-1st c. BCE (Satavahana; caves 9, 10), larger 5th c. CE phase (Vakataka; most of the finest caves + paintings). Types: chaitya-grihas / prayer halls (9, 10, 19, 26) and viharas / monasteries (1, 2, 16, 17). Famed for wall+ceiling murals in natural pigments -- life of the Buddha + Jataka tales; the most important surviving early Indian painting. Forest-covered for centuries; brought to notice 1819 by British officer John Smith on a hunt (his name scratched inside a cave). UNESCO WHS 1983. Site page names nearby: Ellora ~100 km SW, Daulatabad Fort, Bibi ka Maqbara, Aurangabad Caves, Grishneshwar, Lonar Crater Lake. Best Nov-Mar (12-30 C); monsoon lush but harder; summer >40 C; weekdays quieter.
destinationsScraped.access: Air: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) ~100 km. Rail: Jalgaon Jn ~60 km (closest), Aurangabad ~100 km. Road: ~100 km/~2.5h from Aurangabad, ~60 km from Jalgaon, ~100 km from Ellora. Private vehicles park at the T-junction ~4 km away; green ASI shuttle buses run the last stretch to the ticket gate.
destinationsScraped.openingNote: Closed Mondays (standard ASI; the gov page doesn't state it but it is well established). Photography without flash allowed inside; no flash/tripod.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Ticketed ASI WHS, guards + licensed guides, controlled shuttle approach, heavy mixed visitor flow. Long walk, many stairs, cliff-side path with drops -- railings, care in wet monsoon. Hot, little shade on the approach -- water/hat/sun cover. Persistent hawkers + unofficial 'guides' at the T-junction -- book a licensed guide at the gate. Do the day trip from Aurangabad in daylight.

destinationsScraped.name: Ellora Caves
destinationsScraped.summary: 34 rock-cut caves along a ~2 km basalt escarpment ~30 km from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad); excavated ~6th-10th c. CE; Buddhist (12, south), Hindu (17, middle), Jain (5, north) side by side. NEVER lost (unlike Ajanta). Centrepiece: Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) -- a full Dravidian-style Shiva temple cut DOWNWARD from the cliff top, ~200,000 tonnes of rock removed, free-standing temple+courtyard+gateway+elephants+shrines in one piece; the world's largest monolithic rock excavation; attributed to Rashtrakuta king Krishna I, 8th c. Buddhist group incl. the multi-storey Vishvakarma chaitya (Cave 10); Jain Indra Sabha group (30-34) small but finely carved. UNESCO WHS 1983. Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga a short walk away.
destinationsScraped.access: Air/Rail: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) ~30-35 km. Road: ~30 km/~45 min from Aurangabad (passes Daulatabad Fort + Bibi ka Maqbara); ~100 km from Ajanta. Main groups walkable together; ~2 km to the Jain caves at the north end (walk or auto).
destinationsScraped.openingNote: Closed Tuesdays (Ajanta closed Mondays) -- plan the two around that. Photography allowed; interiors dim.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: ASI WHS, guards, ticketing, licensed guides, large mixed flow. Kailasa = stairs, uneven rock, a climb to the rim with UNPROTECTED edges -- care near drops. Hot/unshaded midday outside winter. Walk/auto to the Jain caves is a quieter stretch -- day only, auto if alone. Hawkers + unofficial guides in the car park -- licensed guide from the ticket office only.
destinationsScraped.govPageError: The maharashtratourism.gov.in Ellora page states Ellora 'dates back to the 6th century' only, and that 'John Smith' rediscovered Ellora -- the latter conflates it with Ajanta (Ellora was never lost). Card uses the well-established ~6th-10th c. range and omits the John-Smith-at-Ellora claim.

destinationsScraped.name: Daulatabad Fort (Devgiri)
destinationsScraped.summary: Hill fort ~16 km from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) on the Ellora road, on a 200 m conical hill scarped smooth on its lower slopes. Built 12th c. as Deogiri by Bhillama V (Yadava dynasty), their capital. Defences: concentric walls, a deep moat (said to have held crocodiles), huge iron-spiked anti-elephant gates, a single narrow rock-cut switchback approach incl. the Andheri -- a pitch-dark spiral tunnel built to disorient/trap attackers. 1327: Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq renamed it Daulatabad ('City of Fortune') and force-marched Delhi's population here as his capital; failed within a few years, court returned to Delhi. Later: Bahmanis -> Nizam Shahis of Ahmadnagar -> Mughals (17th c.) -> Marathas. Inside: Chand Minar (~64 m victory tower, 15th c., Alauddin Bahman Shah), Chini Mahal (palace turned state prison, held Abul Hasan Tana Shah of Golconda), Baradari pavilion, cannon towers, summit Deccan view.
destinationsScraped.access: Air/Rail: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) ~20-25 km. Road: ~16 km/~30 min from Aurangabad, on the way to Ellora (~15 km further); Khuldabad + Grishneshwar close. Usually done with Bibi ka Maqbara + Ellora on one Aurangabad day.
destinationsScraped.bestSeason: Oct-Mar (cool); Apr-Jun brutal climb; monsoon slippery path.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Ticketed ASI monument, gate staff, steady mid-morning flow on the main route. Upper fort = long stairways, steep ramps, some exposed edges near the top. The Andheri is a pitch-dark uneven spiral tunnel -- carry your own light, go with others, be firm with men who 'light the way' then demand money at the exit. Hot/unshaded upper climb outside winter. Monkeys snatch food/bags. Morning visit; don't be on the upper fort near closing.

destinationsScraped.name: Bibi ka Maqbara
destinationsScraped.url: https://maharashtratourism.gov.in/heritage/bibi-ka-maqbara/ (read via in-app browser; the gov page is thin -- ~3 sentences + how-to-reach)
destinationsScraped.summary: Mausoleum in a formal Mughal garden ~3-5 km N of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) city. Built in the 1660s for Dilras Banu Begum (titled Rabia-ud-Daurani), first wife of emperor Aurangzeb; commissioned by their son Prince Azam Shah. A deliberate smaller echo of the Taj Mahal -- raised plinth, central bulbous dome, four minarets, arched iwan, charbagh with a long water channel -- but on a tight budget: only the lower part is true marble (from near Jaipur), much of the upper structure is plastered brick/stucco. Hence 'Mini Taj' / 'Taj of the Deccan'. Grave in a sunken chamber open to the sky through a screen. ASI-protected; the city's most-visited single sight. Gov page how-to-reach: airport ~10 km, railway ~5.5 km, ~4 km from the city by ST bus or taxi.
destinationsScraped.access: Air: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar ~10 km. Rail: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar ~5.5 km. Road: ~4 km from the city centre, on the north edge below the Aurangabad Caves. Combine with the Aurangabad Caves (~2 km up the hill) + Panchakki.
destinationsScraped.bestSeason: Oct-Mar; Apr-Jun very hot; monsoon garden green.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Ticketed walled ASI monument in a garden, guards, constant family/tour-group flow, short central auto ride, nothing strenuous (level paths, low plinth). Ordinary city care with auto fares + valuables. Marble steps + tomb chamber slippery in monsoon / when washed. Entrance hawkers + freelance photographers -- firm 'no'. Daylight hours; surrounding roads quieten at night. Gov page names the occupant as 'Rabia-ud-Durrani' (her title); given name Dilras Banu Begum. Commission by Azam Shah + part-marble build are from standard accounts, not the thin gov page.

destinationsScraped.name: Lonar Crater Lake
destinationsScraped.summary: Near-circular meteorite-impact crater ~1.8 km across, ~130-150 m deep, in the basalt lava beds of the Deccan plateau, Buldhana district. Gov page: created ~52,000 years ago (a 2020 argon-dating study argues ~570,000 years -- both noted in the card). The only large impact crater in basaltic rock on Earth; studied by GSI + NASA as a Moon/Mars analogue. Floor holds a shallow lake that is BOTH saline and alkaline, with water layers + microbes found nowhere else. Forested wildlife-rich rim (peafowl, parakeets, migratory birds, langurs, deer, wild boar). Stepped path from rim to water past Hemadpanti/Chalukya-era (6th-12th c.) temples: Daityasudan (Vishnu, in Lonar town, tied to the demon Lonasura the crater is named for), Gomukh (perennial cow-mouth stream, trailhead), Motha Maruti (rock Hanuman idol, high-iron soil), Kamalja Devi (on the rim). Mentioned in the Skanda Purana + Ain-i-Akbari.
destinationsScraped.access: Air: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) ~140 km, Nagpur ~300 km. Rail: no station at Lonar; Jalna / Malkapur / Akola each ~90 km. Road: ~150 km/~3.5h from Aurangabad (the usual base), ~450 km Mumbai, ~300 km Nagpur; MSRTC buses from Aurangabad, Buldhana, Jalna. MTDC Tourist Resort on the crater rim.
destinationsScraped.bestSeason: Oct-Mar; monsoon green but the crater path slippery.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Recognised natural monument, forest-dept presence on the rim, modest steady flow of visitors/students/researchers; MTDC rim resort the reliable base. Descent is a steep uneven scrub path, little shade, few people on a quiet day -- morning, guide/group, not alone late. Own water + sun cover (nothing to buy inside, hot bottom). DO NOT enter the lake (highly alkaline). Keep to marked paths -- rim forest has snakes + langur troops. Remote: nearest hospitals/transport Buldhana or Jalna ~90 km, weak signal on parts of the rim. Time the Aurangabad road transfer for daylight. womenSafety.level Moderate (score 6) for remoteness + the lonely descent.

destinationsScraped.name: Elephanta Caves
destinationsScraped.summary: Rock-cut cave group on a hill on Gharapuri island in Mumbai harbour, ~10 km by sea from the Gateway of India, ~1h ferry. Cut into the island basalt mid-first-millennium CE (most often 6th c.; gov page says 'Gupta, 5th-8th c.'). Predominantly Shaiva Hindu shrines + a couple of minor Buddhist excavations on the eastern hill (gov page overstates the 'Buddhist caves'). Great cave (Cave 1): cruciform pillared hall, cushion-capital columns, nine massive Shiva relief panels (Nataraja, Ardhanarishvara, Shiva-Parvati wedding, Gangadhara, Ravananugraha) around a central linga shrine. South wall: Sadashiva / Maheshamurti -- a 3-faced Shiva bust ~6 m (20 ft) tall, a masterpiece of Indian sculpture. Portuguese (from 16th c.) named the island after a large stone elephant near the landing (now in a Mumbai museum) and left the carvings badly damaged. UNESCO WHS 1987.
destinationsScraped.access: Everything from the Gateway of India ferry jetty, Colaba, Mumbai. Launches ~every 30 min ~9 am-2 pm; last return ~5-5.30 pm; ~1h each way; ferry ~Rs 200-260 return + a small island/ASI entry fee. From the jetty a narrow-gauge toy train covers ~600 m; then ~120 steps up lined with stalls (palanquin for a fee). NO ferries in the monsoon (Jun-Sep, rough harbour).
destinationsScraped.bestSeason: Nov-Feb (cool, calm seas). Ferries suspended in the monsoon.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Busy well-trodden day trip -- shared ferries, staffed ASI site, guides, all-day mixed flow, fixed route. Ferry = open boat on tidal water -- life jacket if provided, don't overcrowd the upper deck, sit when moving, skip it if the sea looks rough. The ~120 steps are lined with pushy stalls + monkeys -- food/phones out of reach, firm with hawkers. CONFIRM the last return ferry and be on it (island empties, no accommodation). Hot/exposed on the boat + steps. Dry bag for tickets/phone/cash.

destinationsScraped.name: Mumbai
destinationsScraped.summary: Capital of Maharashtra, India's financial + entertainment hub, ~20 million on a peninsula in the Arabian Sea; grew from 7 fishing islands. Ptolemy noted a settlement ~150 CE; Portuguese from 1534; to the English Crown in 1661 (Catherine of Braganza's dowry to Charles II); British Bombay -> cotton/shipping/banking hub + freedom-movement centre; state capital from 1960. Tourist core at the southern tip: Gateway of India (1924, marks George V's 1911 visit), Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (UNESCO, 1887, Victorian Gothic Revival + Indian), Kala Ghoda + CSMVS museum, Marine Drive ('Queen's Necklace'), Girgaon Chowpatty. Also Haji Ali Dargah (islet + causeway), Siddhivinayak temple (1801), dhobi ghats, Bandra sea-front, Juhu beach, Elephanta Island, Kanheri Caves in SGNP. Home of Hindi cinema. Street food: vada pav, pav bhaji, bhel/pani/sev puri, bombil fry. Best Oct-Feb (10-35 C); Jun-Sep heavy monsoon (floods); Mar-May hot/humid.
destinationsScraped.access: Air: CSMIA (India's 2nd-busiest). Rail: long-distance at CSMT / Mumbai Central / Dadar / LTT; the suburban local network is the city's lifeline (ladies' compartments + Ladies Special). Road: Mumbai-Pune Expressway. In-city: metro (growing), suburban locals, app cabs, black-and-yellow taxis (south), autos (Bandra northwards only).
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Widely regarded as one of the safest big Indian cities for women -- busy street life late in South Mumbai / Bandra / central areas; ladies' train compartments + Ladies Special; metro + app cabs freely used by women alone; Marine Drive / Colaba Causeway / Gateway crowded well after dark. BUT: rush-hour locals are dangerously overcrowded -- ladies' compartment, no footboard, don't fight the crush; late night prefer app cabs / ladies' compartment over an empty general one. Monsoon (esp. Jul-Aug) = serious flooding + local-train shutdowns -- check forecast, avoid low roads/subways in heavy rain, buffer time. Tide/ferry timings for Elephanta + Haji Ali. Standard bag-watch in station/market crowds; app cabs with live-tracking after dark. Emergency block uses RPF helpline 182 as the 5th entry.

destinationsScraped.name: Kanheri Caves
destinationsScraped.summary: 100+ Buddhist rock-cut caves (gov page: 109) in a basalt hill inside Sanjay Gandhi National Park, ~6 km in from the Borivali gate, northern Mumbai. A working monastery + pilgrimage centre ~1st c. BCE - 10th c. CE (one of the longest continuously occupied Buddhist sites in western India), sustained by trade routes to Sopara + Kalyan ports. Mostly viharas -- cells with rock-cut beds around pillared halls, linked by stairways, served by cut channels + cisterns harvesting monsoon runoff. Showpiece: Cave 3, the Great Chaitya -- large apsidal prayer hall, ribbed vault, 2 rows of columns, stupa at the apse, colossal standing Buddhas flanking the porch. Other caves: seated/standing Buddhas, Bodhisattva reliefs, Brahmi inscriptions. (Gov page's 'Maurya and Gupta empires' / '1,100-1,000 years ago' is imprecise -- card uses the standard 1st c. BCE - 10th c. CE.)
destinationsScraped.access: Borivali station (Western Line local) is the access point; autos to the SGNP Borivali gate; from the gate ~6 km to the caves by the park bus or a permitted vehicle (private cars not always allowed to the caves). ~15-20 km from CSMIA. Park entry fee + bus/vehicle charge.
destinationsScraped.bestSeason: Nov-Feb; monsoon green but slippery rock + leeches.
destinationsScraped.safetyNotes: Ticketed ASI monument inside a gated staffed national park, steady visitor/student/jogger flow esp. weekend mornings, Cave 3 area open + busy. SGNP HAS ONE OF THE HIGHEST LEOPARD DENSITIES anywhere near a city -- leopards active dawn/dusk/night on the forest roads + edges; visit in daylight, stay with others, keep to the marked route, DON'T walk the 6 km park road alone early or late. Upper caves = steep worn rock stairs, drops, no railings in places, slippery when wet. Quiet away from Cave 3 -- outlying cells with a companion. Own water + sun cover. Morning trip; back at the gate well before dusk. womenSafety.level Safe (score 7).
